findings.highlight: After all, I am her yes-man here.
findings.evidenceJa: なんて、それも当然だ。何しろあの人の受け売りなんだから。
findings.explanation: Haruki realizes that Hamada's noble declaration is naturally reminiscent of Mari because Hamada has just repeated words borrowed from her after her international call. The English instead calls Haruki Mari's yes-man, changing both the person being described and the point of the reveal.
findings.japanese:
なんて、それも当然だ。
何しろあの人の受け売りなんだから。
findings.todokanai: Who am I kidding, that's only natural. After all, I am her yes-man here.

findings.highlight: He's been sitting on the fence for the past five years!
findings.evidenceJa: 「ほんっと酷い人だよね春希くんって。五年間もずっとふたまたかけ続けてさぁ！」
findings.explanation: Setsuna accuses Haruki of two-timing Kazusa and her continuously for five years. 'Sitting on the fence' turns sustained romantic betrayal into mere indecision and strips the accusation of its sexual and relational force.
findings.japanese:
「ほんっと酷い人だよね春希くんって。
五年間もずっとふたまたかけ続けてさぁ！」
findings.todokanai: "Haruki-kun really is a cruel person, isn't he? He's been sitting on the fence for the past five years!"

findings.highlight: you think you're winning his favor by trying to help me up on my feet again
findings.evidenceJa: 「お前があたしに構うのは、あいつがそうするからだろ？あたしを立ち直らせることが、あいつに尽くすことだって思ってるんだろ？」
findings.explanation: Kazusa asks whether Setsuna believes restoring her is a way of devoting herself to Haruki—doing for him what he would do. 'Winning his favor' instead imputes a calculated attempt to ingratiate herself with him, materially changing Setsuna's motive and Kazusa's accusation.
findings.japanese:
「お前があたしに構うのは、あいつがそうするからだろ？
あたしを立ち直らせることが、
あいつに尽くすことだって思ってるんだろ？」
findings.todokanai: "The reason that you're concerned about me is because he himself is concerned about me, right? And you think you're winning his favor by trying to help me up on my feet again, don't you?"

findings.highlight: when you're the one lacking in skill
findings.evidenceJa: 「居眠りしてる客を目覚めさせてこそプロだろ？認めてくれないのは相手が悪いなんて、努力不足の言い訳でしかないな」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says blaming an unreceptive audience is merely an excuse for insufficient effort. The English changes 努力不足 into lack of skill, contradicting the scene's sustained argument about effort, understanding, and professional responsibility.
findings.japanese:
「居眠りしてる客を目覚めさせてこそプロだろ？
認めてくれないのは相手が悪いなんて、
努力不足の言い訳でしかないな」
findings.todokanai: "A true pro would be able to awaken the audience from their sleep, no? It's nothing but an excuse to blame the people who won't give you the light of day when you're the one lacking in skill."

findings.highlight: This time, I'll capture the hearts of your audience.
findings.evidenceJa: 「追加公演を見てなさい。今度こそかずさの…観客の心、掴んでみせるから」
findings.explanation: Setsuna starts to say that this time she will capture Kazusa's heart, then corrects herself to the audience's heart. The English smooths the broken syntax into 'your audience' and erases the revealing romantic slip that makes Kazusa invite her upstairs for an encore.
findings.japanese:
「追加公演を見てなさい。
今度こそかずさの…
観客の心、掴んでみせるから」
findings.todokanai: "Just wait until the additional concert. This time, I'll capture the hearts of your audience."

findings.highlight: If you're going to rile me up, I won't be heading back until morning.
findings.evidenceJa: 「っ！…一度上がり込んだら朝まで帰らないに決まってるから、せっかく遠慮してたのになぁ」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she had been holding back out of consideration because, once she went up to Kazusa's room, she knew she would not leave until morning. The English invents retaliation for being riled up and loses the admission that her apparent retreat was deliberate restraint.
findings.japanese:
「っ！
…一度上がり込んだら朝まで帰らないに決まってるから、
せっかく遠慮してたのになぁ」
findings.todokanai: "…! If you're going to rile me up, I won't be heading back until morning. And here I was actually being considerate of you."
